findings.title: Hung flusher processes are never killed before being replaced
findings.body: Processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, whose SpawnProcess objects are not instances of multiprocessing.Process (the fork-context Process class). The new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard therefore evaluates to False for every real flusher process. When _ensure_processes_alive detects a hang (is_alive() is True but healthy_since is stale), it skips process.kill() and immediately calls _create_process_for_shards for the same shards. The hung process keeps running alongside its replacement, so two processes can concurrently call flush_segments/done_flush_segments and produce for the same Redis shards, risking duplicate or racing segment flushes, while the hung process continues consuming resources. The guard should check against the spawn context's process type / BaseProcess, or duck-type on kill/terminate.

findings.title: join() never terminates spawned flusher processes
findings.body: join() uses the same isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check before calling process.terminate(). Because the flushers are SpawnProcess objects from the spawn context, this check is always False in production, so any flusher that does not exit promptly after stopped is set is never terminated. join() waits until the deadline for each process in sequence and then silently returns with daemon processes still alive, leaking processes and potentially leaving flushers running against Redis/Kafka after the consumer strategy has shut down. Use the mp_context process base type or hasattr-based termination instead.

findings.title: Negative or zero flusher-process configuration crashes or disables flushing
findings.body: The CLI option --flusher-processes accepts any int with no validation. A negative value flows through factory.py into SpanFlusher, where max_processes stays negative (only 0/None fall back via `or`), num_processes = min(negative, len(shards)) is negative, process_to_shards_map is empty, and the shard assignment loop then raises KeyError/ZeroDivision-style failures when computing i % num_processes or indexing the map. If assigned_shards is empty, num_processes is 0 and no flusher process is ever created while submit() still forwards messages to the committer, so spans can be committed to Redis but never flushed. Validate flusher_processes >= 1 at the CLI/factory boundary and handle the no-shards case explicitly.

findings.title: Multiprocess flusher test never exercises flushing or restart with multiple processes
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts len(processes)/num_processes and that the shard map totals 4, then immediately joins without submitting any span or advancing drift, so it cannot catch regressions in per-process flushing, duplicate production when shards share a process, backpressure aggregation, or the process-restart path in _ensure_processes_alive. Given the PR's core change is parallel flushing and supervision, a test should push spans through a multi-process (at least multi-thread via produce_to_pipe) flusher and assert each segment is produced exactly once, and/or simulate a dead/hung process and assert it is replaced.
